Am I ready?

Four questions. An honest answer.

Most people who ask are more ready than they think. If you're not quite there yet, we'll tell you, and show you how to get there.

Question 1 of 4How long can you comfortably hike today?
Question 2 of 4How do you feel on steep, exposed ground?
Question 3 of 4Have you ever used crampons or a rope?
Question 4 of 4What's the highest you've hiked?

    Your guide

    Follow the red jacket.

    Every Northvale guide wears rust, so on a crowded hut terrace or a glacier in a whiteout, you always know who to look for. Here's what that person is doing for you all day.

    1. Reads the mountainChecks the forecast at 5 a.m., the snow at every bend, and picks the line that's safest that day, not just on paper.
    2. Ropes you inTies every knot, checks every harness, and stays on the rope with you across anything with a drop.
    3. Turns back when it's rightA summit is optional; coming home isn't. If conditions change, your guide makes the call, and you get credit toward a future trip.
    MFMarco FehrGuiding since 2009 · Glacier and summit
    LBLea BrunnerGuiding since 2014 · Trek and glacier
    AKAnja KesslerGuiding since 2011 · Summit
    What's included

    Bring your boots. We'll bring the mountain kit.

    Every trip includes your guide, the huts, and the meals. Bring your own technical gear, or rent it from us and pick it up on day one.

    Included
    • IFMGA guide for the whole trip
    • Every hut night, with dinner and breakfast
    • Ropes and group safety gear
    • Transfers back to the valley
    You bring
    • Broken-in mountain boots
    • Waterproof jacket and warm layers
    • Sunglasses, sunscreen, and a 35-liter pack

    Technical kit: bring your own, or switch on rental above.
